simple.meaning: תָּאַם (tâʼam) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be (causatively, make ) twinned , i.e. (figuratively) duplicate or (architectural) jointed.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in Exodus, Song of Solomon, beginning at Exodus 26:24. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תָּאַם (H8382) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: תָּאַם (tâʼam) / H8382 is traced through Exodus 26:24, Exodus 36:29, Song of Songs 4:2, Song of Songs 6:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

structuredEvidence.definition: to be (causatively, make ) twinned , i.e. (figuratively) duplicate or (architectural) jointed

firstOccurrence.englishText: They shall be double beneath, and in the same way they shall be whole to its top to one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the two corners.

timeline.evidenceText: They shall be double beneath, and in the same way they shall be whole to its top to one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the two corners.
They were double beneath, and in the same way they were all the way to its top to one ring. He did this to both of them in the two corners.
